title: Al-Qudwah as-Samitah: Your Child Imitates What They See You Do
summary: The strongest tarbiyah (upbringing) at this age is not through words but through imitation. Your child is programmed to mimic what they see you do: when they see you pray, say 'Bismillah,' smile at people, or help others—they store that as a model. You don’t need lessons; you need to *be* the lesson. Let your child see you in your worship with serenity, say your adhkar (remembrances) in a gentle, audible voice, and interact with the akhlaq (character) you want them to learn. The silent qudwah (example) plants deeper than a thousand commands because a child believes what they see far more than what they are told.
try_this: This week: Let your child see you pray or remember Allah with tranquility once daily without asking them to do anything. Observe whether they begin to imitate your movements or words spontaneously.
reflection_prompts: What behavior do you want your child to learn—do they see it in you first?
How can you make your daily acts of worship a beautiful sight that your child will love to imitate?
